title: Rotary Vacuum Pump

introduction.definition: An oil-sealed rotary vane vacuum pump traps gas between vanes in an eccentric chamber, compresses it to just above atmospheric pressure and expels it through an exhaust valve under oil. The oil seals clearances so it reaches rough-to-medium vacuum.
key_points: Gas ballast prevents vapour condensing in the oil
introduction.summary: An oil-sealed rotary vane vacuum pump draws gas from a vessel by trapping it between vanes in an eccentric chamber, compressing it to just above atmospheric pressure and expelling it through an oil-covered exhaust valve. The oil seals the small clearances, which lets these pumps reach a rough to medium vacuum (typically down to ~0.1 mbar or below for two-stage designs).

steps.text: Gas from the vessel enters through the inlet as the cell grows.
The vanes sweep the gas round and compress it.
When above atmospheric pressure the exhaust valve opens under the oil.
Gas passes the oil box and demister to atmosphere; the oil is retained.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Pumping speed nearly constant from atmosphere down to ~1 mbar, then falls toward the ultimate pressure.

foundation: Mount on a rigid, level foundation or grouted baseplate sized for the machine mass and dynamic loads (typically ≥3–5 × machine mass for reciprocating machines).
Check for soft foot before final bolting.
alignment: Align driver and driven shafts with a laser or dial-indicator method to the coupling maker's tolerances; re-check hot alignment where thermal growth is significant.
piping: Keep inlet line short and of full size; fit an inlet trap/filter for dust and condensables.
Pipe the exhaust away from occupied areas.
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

periodic.task: Run with gas ballast to purge vapours.

overhaul.task: Replace vanes, shaft seal and exhaust valve.

lubrication: Vacuum pump oil (low vapour pressure); never use ordinary lube oil.

causes: Saturated demister, high inlet pressure for long periods

video_tutorials.title: Rotary Vacuum Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Rotary Vacuum Pump.
An oil-sealed rotary vane vacuum pump traps gas between vanes in an eccentric chamber, compresses it to just above atmospheric pressure and expels it through an exhaust valve under oil.
The oil seals clearances so it reaches rough-to-medium vacuum.
Typical applications include laboratory and vacuum furnaces; packaging and vacuum forming; refrigeration evacuation; backing pump for high-vacuum pumps.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Pump Stator (Cylinder) with Ports, Slotted Rotor & Shaft (eccentric), Vane 1, Vane 2.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Rotary Vacuum Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Rotary Vacuum Pump.
Check oil level and colour.
Change oil and exhaust filter.
Run with gas ballast to purge vapours.
Replace vanes, shaft seal and exhaust valve.
Watch for poor ultimate vacuum: cannot reach pressure. Common cause: contaminated oil, leaks, worn vanes.
Watch for oil mist at exhaust: smoke. Common cause: saturated demister, high inlet pressure for long periods.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: Why is the pump "oil-sealed"?
options: Oil seals the clearances so lower pressure is reached

questions.question: What is the gas-ballast valve for?

options: Water/vapour contamination — change oil, use gas ballast
